notes: rebase-verify reads each command up to its first 240 characters, so a check at the end of a long chained command can be missed.

Paths are compared lower-cased, with a backslash read as a forward slash, and are read relative to the project folder of the session, so a folder above the project named test or specs changes nothing.
Sessions with no time are left out, as they cannot be placed in a month.
Leading environment assignments and runner wrappers such as npx, uv run, python -m and pnpm exec are skipped before a command is matched.

Two runs count as the same check when their command words match: the words before the first flag or path, wrappers dropped, so a narrower run of the same check (pytest tests/a.py after pytest) is the same command.
A failed command that holds a check counts as a failed check, and in a chain such as npm test && git push the exit status cannot say which part failed, so the chain counts as its first check.
Options that list files or statistics instead of the diff, such as git diff --stat and --name-only, and git show <rev>:<path>, are not read as a diff appearing.

practices.definition: After the last file edit before a git commit, a check ran in the session: tests, a linter, a type check or a build.
Both a source file and a test file were edited in the session.
practices.denominator: Sessions that edited a source file.

practices.definition: A check command (tests, a linter, a type check or a build) failed, files were edited, and then the same check succeeded in the session.
practices.denominator: Sessions where a check command failed.

practices.definition: A planning step came before the first file edit in the session: plan mode, a task list, or writing a plan or spec file.
Before a commit or a pull request, the diff appeared in the session (git diff, git show or gh pr diff), whoever asked for it; the session cannot show whether anyone read it.
practices.denominator: Sessions with a commit or a pull request.

practices.definition: A design document (an ADR, RFC, spec or design file, by path) was written or edited in the session.
A dependency audit or a security scanner ran in the session.
asks for options or trade-offs before choosing one
negative: What does this function return when the list is empty?
positive: Before we pick a queue library, give me two or three options with their trade-offs.
Is there another way to do this besides a cron job? Compare them for me.
practices.tone: Tone, feelings, politeness and wording quality are never grounds for a yes.

practices.definition: rejects or corrects what the agent proposed or did, and says why
negative: Why did you choose a map here instead of a list?
positive: No, don't mock the database here: the bug was in the real query, so the test would hide it.
That rename breaks the public API for existing users, revert it.
practices.tone: Tone, feelings, politeness and wording quality are never grounds for a yes.

practices.definition: states acceptance criteria, the expected behaviour, or the check that proves it
negative: Make sure it works properly when you are done.
positive: Done when the export returns all rows and the integration test for empty results passes.
It should redirect to /login when the session expires; I'll check that by hand.
practices.tone: Tone, feelings, politeness and wording quality are never grounds for a yes.

practices.definition: cuts, splits or defers part of the work explicitly
negative: Do the backend and the UI and the docs.
Can you also look at the other files while you are there?
positive: Only do the backend for now; leave the UI for a separate change.
Skip the refactor, just fix the crash in this PR.
practices.tone: Tone, feelings, politeness and wording quality are never grounds for a yes.
